This one is a bit tricky. "هر کسی آن دَ رَ وَ د عاقبت کار که کشت" – maybe "Everyone has the end of their work as they sowed" or "Each person reaps what they sow." Like "you reap what you sow, so if I'm good or bad, you should take care of yourself." Not sure. Maybe it's saying that regardless of whether I'm good or bad, you should focus on yourself.

Translation: "If there were people without flaws, where would they be? What flaw is this that from that flaw there will be a defect?" Wait, maybe "If there were people without flaws, where would they be? What kind of flaw is this that from that flaw there will be a defect?" Hmm. So the idea is that no one is without flaws, so pointing out a flaw in someone else is not a big deal because everyone has flaws. So maybe it's saying that it's normal to have flaws, so don't worry about it.

"Clean yourself first, then look at the purity of others. I washed with tears, the wayfarers say." Wait, maybe "First purify yourself, then look at others' purity. Option 4: Purify yourself first before judging others.
